paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of FOCUS values across political leanings
model_annotation: This stacked bar chart illustrates the distribution of FOCUS values across various political leanings. The horizontal axis displays the categories of political sources, labeled from left to right as "Left bias", "Left center bias", "Quest. source", and "Right bias", with the text rotated diagonally. The vertical axis represents the distribution proportion on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 0.2. The chart features four vertical stacked bars, each reaching a uniform total height of 1.0, representing the full distribution for each category. Every bar is divided into three vertically stacked segments corresponding to categories identified in a legend positioned to the left of the chart area: "HERO" at the bottom in dark blue, "VICTIM" in the middle in brown, and "VILLAIN" at the top in light blue. For the dark blue "HERO" segments, approximate heights range from 0.26 in "Right bias" to 0.45 in "Quest. source". The brown "VICTIM" segments measure roughly 0.14 in both "Left bias" and "Right bias", while reaching its tallest point of about 0.20 in "Left center bias" and its shortest point of 0.05 in "Quest. source". The light blue "VILLAIN" segments extend to the 1.0 mark at the top of every bar, yielding lengths ranging from approximately 0.45 in "Left center bias" to about 0.60 in "Right bias". The main category bars do not follow a strict alphabetical or ascending/descending numerical sorting order, and there are no visual emphasis elements such as outlines, shading, or individual data annotations applied to the bars.
